about.title: Stanton Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Stanton residents rely daily on cars, appliances, tools, and consumer goods that are supposed to work as intended. When a manufacturing flaw, design defect, or missing warning causes harm, California's strict liability rules often let an injured person pursue compensation without proving the manufacturer was negligent — only that the product was defective and caused the injury. This matters in a city like Stanton, tucked into a busy stretch of Orange County along corridors such as Beach Boulevard and Katella Avenue, where household products, vehicles, and workplace equipment all see heavy daily use. If a defective product hurt you here, the item itself becomes central evidence, so preserving it matters. LawProactive doesn't practice law — we connect Stanton residents at no cost with an independent attorney experienced in defective product claims, so you can focus on recovery while someone else sorts out the legal steps. There's no fee unless the attorney recovers compensation for you.

items.question: I was hurt by a product near Beach Boulevard in Stanton — what should I do with it?
items.answer: Keep the product exactly as it was when the injury happened, including any packaging, parts, or receipts. Don't attempt repairs or throw it away, since it's often the most important evidence in a defective product claim. An attorney can advise on proper storage and next steps.

items.question: Do I have to prove the manufacturer was negligent?
items.answer: Not necessarily. California generally allows strict liability claims, meaning you often only need to show the product was defective — through design, manufacturing, or an inadequate warning — and that the defect caused your injury.
